# uapi_cron_job (Data Source)

Look up a root crontab entry by id, as crond reads it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "uapi_cron_job" "nightly_reboot" {
  id = "0a1b2c3d4e5f"
}

output "crond_running" {
  value = data.uapi_cron_job.nightly_reboot.runtime.crond_running
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) Resource id to look up.

### Read-Only

- `command` (String) The command as crond runs it: lines ending in `\` joined to the next, cut at the first `#`, surrounding whitespace stripped.
- `runtime` (Attributes) Live crond state (read-only). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--runtime))
- `schedule` (String) The five time fields as crond reads them, joined by single spaces.

<a id="nestedatt--runtime"></a>
### Nested Schema for `runtime`

Read-Only:

- `crond_running` (Boolean) Whether procd reports a running crond. False means no entry runs, whatever the file says: the init script does not start crond while `/etc/crontabs` is empty, and stops it when `system.cronloglevel` is invalid. Null when procd could not be asked.
- `runs_as_written` (Boolean) False when crond runs this schedule differently from how it reads, such as minute 75 (every minute), weekday 7 (every day) or `@daily` (never). uapi refuses such a schedule on write, so only another writer can leave one.
